label: Ramesses III's temple in the forecourt
more: Ramesses III (reigned about 1184 to 1153 BC) built a complete small temple as a bark shrine, a station for the portable boats of Amun, Mut and Khonsu on festival days. Shoshenq I's court later enclosed its front part.

label: Shoshenq I's campaign relief
more: Shoshenq I carved his campaign into Canaan beside the south-east doorway of his court: the king smiting enemies above rings naming about 156 towns. He is usually identified with the Bible's Shishak, though Jerusalem is missing from the surviving list.

label: Taharqa's kiosk
more: Taharqa, a Kushite king from Nubia, raised a kiosk of ten papyrus columns, each about 21 metres tall, in Shoshenq I's court. Only one column stands. Its purpose is unclear, and it was probably never roofed.
